newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on Nikkei gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs subside on Nikkei gains.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures subsided on Wednesday as players cashed in some of their recent gains following a late bout of short-covering in the Nikkei.
Dealers said the Japanese interest rate market remained on an uptrend amid persistent indications of a weak economy and a low interest rate environment for the foreseeable future.
"There's no confirmation that the trend is reversed. I'm still looking at good JGBs and a weak Nikkei," a senior trader at a European institution said.
The 225-share Nikkei average rebounded from a low of 19,233.12 to end at 19,702.07, 187.62 points above its previous close.
"The JGB market has gone up like a bullet. Today we just saw some profit-taking," the trader said.
September JGBs ended at 126.05 after hitting a high of 126.65 against a previous 126.41.
The lead March Euroyen contract stood at its day low of 99.15 at 1110 GMT after hitting a high of 99.18 against an IMM close at 99.16.
Eurodollar futures recovered from early lows in line with gains in U.S. treasuries in London on expectations of a positive 10-year note auction later in the day.
December Eurodollars and March Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM closes at 94.075 and 93.985 respectively.
